title: KV page fragmentation, compaction and cross-GPU migration policy
creator: Priya Sharma
description: Problem: As workloads with diverse sequence lengths and multi-tenant mixing run on dedicated pools, the paged KV cache shows increasing internal fragmentation across page blocks and sub-blocks on GPUs. This causes: higher GPU memory pressure, extra host<->device staging during spills, and poorer effective batching because requests touch many small fragments. Goal: define a deterministic fragmentation metric, design an online compaction strategy that runs concurrently with inference, and implement a cross-GPU migration policy for hot shards to avoid OOMs and reduce spills. This ticket covers spec, prototype, tests, performance targets, observability and rollout plan for the compaction + migration subsystem.
acceptance_criteria: Define fragmentation score (per-allocator and per-page) and surface it as a new telemetry metric
Implement background compaction that can run without blocking token generation and reduces fragmentation by >= 40% on heavy-mix benchmarks
Add a migration decision module that moves hot KV pages to less-loaded GPUs with minimal added latency (tail 99.9% increase < 5ms for affected requests)
Provide integration tests that simulate mixed sequence workloads and assert no regressions in p50/p95 latency and that memory spills fall by >= 30%
Dashboard with per-tenant fragmentation, compaction runs, migration events, and cost estimate for migrations exposed in Console
notes: We intentionally avoid global stop-the-world compaction. Prototype uses a lock-free page-relocation scheme with lightweight epoch checks and copy-on-write for in-flight KV references. Migration is throttled by a token-bucket to avoid cascading hot-move storms across a pool.
rollout_plan: 1) Canary compaction module in non-critical pool (1 host) for 2 weeks
2) Enable migration decisions as telemetry-only (no automatic moves) for additional 1 week to validate heuristics
3) Enable automatic migration with conservative throttles within a single availability zone
4) Gradually increase allowed migration bandwidth and lower compaction thresholds based on observed metrics
tests: unit: allocator fragmentation invariants and fallback paths
integration: multi-GPU mixed-sequence synthetic workload (1000QPS, sequences 32-4096)
e2e: dedicated pool soak test under spike patterns (24h)
observability_plan: emit per-page fragmentation_score, last_compacted_ts, origin_gpu, desired_gpu
trace compaction duration and bytes moved as spans
alert if compaction frequency > 1/min without fragmentation reduction
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: compaction can increase latency if run synchronously -> Mitigation: run in background worker with latency budget and pause on SLO pressure
Risk: migration storms -> Mitigation: global throttling and hysteresis, prefer local evictions first
Risk: CPU overhead for compaction on host -> Mitigation: offload page copy to DMA and limit compaction CPU budget
